tasks.task: Write volunteer role descriptions for a programme

items.when: When one task needs a one-page role that sets expectations without reading like a job contract
When the group's whole task list must become a set of roles with check points marked
When roles, screening, training and shifts are all unclear and need sorting first

tasks.task: Write a call for volunteers and the sign-up reply

items.when: When you need website text, a social post, flyer text and the reply, all saying the same thing
When the call opens with 'volunteers needed' and you want several stronger first lines
When the call must be reworked for each social platform the group uses
When the call goes on a noticeboard and must read from across the room without photos
Before posting, to read the call as a stranger and see if time, place and next step are clear
When the ask leans on guilt and needs real proof and an honest, small first step

tasks.task: Build a volunteer welcome and induction pack

items.when: When a person signs up and you need every step from reply to their second shift
When new volunteers need a welcome pack with safeguarding and check points marked
When the group has its own procedures and needs an induction list, practice plan and supervision gaps
When the induction is a live session and needs planning minute by minute
After inductions run, to check what each volunteer has really been shown and signed off

tasks.task: Set screening and safeguarding steps for each role

items.when: When each role needs its screening steps and training written beside it
When roles near children or adults at risk must have their checks marked in the pack
Before the pack goes out, to tie each check you name to a dated official source

tasks.task: Plan a volunteer rota and cover for no-shows

items.when: When busy hours and each person's limits are known and you want cover checked per option
When the rota needs a fair pattern for weekends and a simple swap rule
When a charity shop mixes paid staff and volunteers and needs trained roles and backup cover

tasks.task: Plan how to thank and keep volunteers through the year

items.when: When you need the year's thank-you moments, check-ins and a short exit question
When one person deserves a short note with one true, specific thank-you and no ask
When volunteers go quiet or drift away and you need the likely reasons in order
When the plan is badges and prizes and may crowd out why people came
When the programme starts well and fades, to tie the work to daily local needs

tasks.task: Turn sign-in sheets into an hours and impact report

items.when: When you have sign-in sheets and need hours, people and what the work made possible
When dated sign-in records need a monthly summary with counts you can trace back
When nobody has agreed what to count, who tracks it and when
When the report needs one real story told with consent and checked facts
When the numbers are ready and need a point, the proof and a next step for trustees
Before it goes to funders, to tie every number and claim to a record

tasks.task: Prepare a hard conversation with a volunteer or member

items.when: When someone's behaviour must be raised and you need an opening built on facts
When two members or volunteers have fallen out and you need ground rules and what to say

tasks.task: Write the welcome messages for new members

items.when: When the club needs its full member message set with timing and channel
Before writing, to compare three plans for the welcome series, each with its first email
When you need the first weeks staged, with a clear first thing each member should do
When the series needs full emails with subject lines and send timing
When an email is drafted, to get cuts, subject fixes and a score before sending

tasks.task: Run renewal season with reminders and a last call

items.when: Six to eight weeks before the deadline, to set the steps, dates and who does what
When you need the invitation, reminders, failed payment note, last call and lapsed note
When reminders repeat themselves and each needs a new reason and a stop rule
When renewal emails go unopened and you want subject lines in several angles
When members leave at renewal and you need a plan for failed payments and reasons to stay
Before the first send, to test that a member can really renew and pay from the link today

tasks.task: Write to lapsed members and learn why they left

items.when: When a lapsed-member note is needed that is warm and asks one question
When members also give, to plan thank-yous and a route back for those who lapsed
When one note is not enough, to compare three shapes for a short win-back series
Before sending, to cut anything that reads as a guilt trip

tasks.task: Write the join page, membership tiers and sign-up form

items.when: When the club is unsure about tiers, prices or a pay-per-visit option
When the join page is being redone, to see three different first screens as real pages
When the sign-up form needs its fields, error messages and spam protection set
When people start the join form and give up part way
Before sharing the link, to test that a new person can join and pay today
When the group wants more members and needs a plan to grow and turn members into advocates

tasks.task: Prepare an AGM notice, agenda and papers

items.when: When the committee sets a date and you need every step and deadline up to the minutes
When you need a notice and agenda that follow the group's own constitution
When the pack needs papers, nominations and a proxy form where the rules allow
When officer roles and committee duties are unclear before the elections
Before the notice goes out, to tie each date and voting rule to a clause in the constitution
When meetings are run by the loudest voices and members stop coming

tasks.task: Write minutes from rough notes or a transcript

items.when: After a committee meeting or AGM, to record decisions, votes and actions
When a charity board needs minutes in a formal layout that follows the agenda
When an informal meeting just needs short minutes with owners and dates
Before the next meeting, to check last time's actions and build the agenda from what is open
When committee meetings drift and need a pre-read and a clear reason to meet

tasks.task: Write club rules or a code of conduct on one page

items.when: When the club needs plain rules that match its constitution
When a rule has changed and members or volunteers need it explained with a short notice
When the rules read like a legal document and members will not get through them

tasks.task: Write a member newsletter issue

items.when: When the newsletter has no fixed sections, reader groups or schedule yet
When notes arrive each week or month and the issue should be drafted and checked the same way
Before sending, to get subject lines in several angles
When the issue is drafted, to get cuts and a score before it goes out

tasks.task: Write a new member welcome pack

items.when: When the pack must match what the welcome messages promise
When new members ask the same things and the pack needs a questions section
When the club will lay out and update the pack itself
Before it is sent, to read the pack as a brand-new member and list what is missing

tasks.task: Run a member or volunteer survey and brief the committee

items.when: When questions are drafted, to remove leading wording and plan a small pretest
When results are in, to see which answers can be trusted
When the committee needs a findings table with honest caveats about who answered

tasks.task: Handle member data, consent and data requests

items.when: When the club collects member details and has no privacy wording to show them
When a member asks for a copy of their data or to be removed

tasks.task: Plan a volunteer day or member event

items.when: When the event needs step-free access planned from arrival to exit, with venue questions
When the event must fill places and have a follow-up for those who came
When you have the details and need a poster layout and an export checklist

tasks.task: Recruit committee members and hand over officer roles

items.when: When seats are open and you need the skills wanted, a plan and welcome steps
When a chair, secretary or lead is stepping down and cover is needed
When the outgoing officer must leave a note the next person can run from

tasks.task: Report membership and renewal numbers to the committee

items.when: When the same member numbers are needed each month in a report you can rerun
When the report must ask the committee for clear decisions, not just show figures
Before the meeting, to tie each figure to the member list it came from

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real group, its constitution and its tools
Before anything goes to members or volunteers, to cut it to plain, friendly words
Whenever the work states a rule, a date or a legal duty, to give it a source or cut it

helpers.when: When the job turns into an appeal, a grant bid or donor care
When a volunteer day or AGM needs a venue, a run sheet and suppliers
When the call for volunteers or welcome pack needs a designed flyer or layout
When a recruitment drive needs a run of posts, not one
When renewal messages need list set-up, automation and results tracking
When subscriptions, the treasurer's report or the club accounts need sorting

gaps: No library item builds a volunteer rota from people's availability; the shift items are written for paid staff
No library item covers safeguarding or tracks background checks and their renewal dates
No library item writes a club constitution, club rules or a code of conduct
No library item covers AGM steps such as notice periods, nominations, proxies and votes beyond the kit
No library item writes member renewal messages; the nearest items are for donors and shop customers
No library item designs a member or volunteer survey; the survey designer is for employees
No library item turns sign-in sheets into a volunteer hours report or plans a year of thank-yous beyond the kit skill
No library item writes a welcome pack or makes different versions of one to compare
No library item writes a treasurer's report or a simple club accounts summary
No library item checks the line between a volunteer and a worker
No library item makes clearly different versions of a hard conversation plan or a member newsletter layout
The library has no tool guide for a membership database or a mailing tool
